title.en: Compute the rate of inflation and real wage
List issues in constructing index numbers and their uses

say.en: "Sensex jumps 600 points." "Inflation eases to 5 per cent." "Industrial output grows." Every evening the news reads out index numbers. Let us decode them. In this lesson: Describe WPI, IIP and Sensex.
Compute the rate of inflation and real wage.
List issues in constructing index numbers and their uses.

body.en: The Wholesale Price *Index* (WPI, base 2011–12) measures changes in the general price level of goods; it has no reference consumer group and does not include services. The Index of Industrial Production (IIP, base 2011–12) measures changes in the volume of industrial output. The Sensex of the Bombay Stock Exchange (base 1978–79 = 100) is based on 30 leading shares. The rate of inflation is $\frac{I_1 - I_0}{I_0}\times 100$.
body.kn: ಸಗಟು ಬೆಲೆ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ ಸರಕುಗಳ ಸಗಟು ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ಉತ್ಪಾದನಾ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆಯ ಪರಿಮಾಣ ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಸೆನ್ಸೆಕ್ಸ್ 30 ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಷೇರುಗಳನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿದೆ. ಬೆಲೆ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕದ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯೇ ಹಣದುಬ್ಬರ.

title.en: From index to inflation and real wage

narration.en: The teacher shows the main Indian indices as cards, then computes inflation and a real wage.

say.en: Four indices you hear about in the news.
Inflation is the percentage change in a price index. If WPI goes from 120 to 126, inflation is 5 percent.
Real wage removes the effect of prices: money wage divided by CPI, times one hundred.
And purchasing power of a rupee is one hundred over the CPI: at 125, a rupee buys what 80 paise bought in the base year.
The teacher shows the main Indian indices as cards, then computes inflation and a real wage.

title.en: Inflation and the value of money

caption.en: The inflation rate is the percentage change in a price index from one year to the next. The purchasing power of a rupee is 100 ÷ CPI (in base-year rupees), and real income is money income × 100 ÷ CPI.
caption.kn: ಹಣದುಬ್ಬರ ದರ ಬೆಲೆ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕದ ವಾರ್ಷಿಕ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ. ರೂಪಾಯಿಯ ಖರೀದಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ 100 ÷ CPI; ನೈಜ ಆದಾಯ = ಹಣದ ಆದಾಯ × 100 ÷ CPI.

body.en: While constructing an index we must decide its purpose, choose a normal base year, select representative items, decide on the prices (wholesale or retail) and their source, and choose weights. *Index numbers* are used to measure inflation, to deflate money values into real values (real wage, real GDP), to fix dearness allowance and wages, and to guide government policy.
body.kn: ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ ರಚಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲು ಉದ್ದೇಶ, ಆಧಾರ ವರ್ಷ, ವಸ್ತುಗಳು, ಬೆಲೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ತೂಕಗಳನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸಬೇಕು. ಹಣದುಬ್ಬರ ಅಳೆಯಲು, ನೈಜ ವೇತನ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಲು, ತುಟ್ಟಿಭತ್ಯೆ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಲು ಮತ್ತು ನೀತಿ ರಚನೆಗೆ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕಗಳು ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ.

problem.en: A worker's wage rose from ₹12,000 (CPI 120) to ₹15,000 (CPI 150). Has her real wage risen?

steps.en: Money wage rose 25% but prices also rose 25% (120 → 150).
So the real wage is unchanged.

answer.en: No: her real wage stayed at ₹10,000

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A worker's wage rose from ₹12,000 (CPI 120) to ₹15,000 (CPI 150). Has her real wage risen?

say.en: Let us work this out together. A worker's wage rose from 12,000 rupees CPI 120 to 15,000 rupees CPI 150. Has her real wage risen?
Real wage before equals 12,000 divided by 120 times 100 equals 10,000 rupees.
Real wage now equals 15,000 divided by 150 times 100 equals 10,000 rupees.
Money wage rose 25 percent but prices also rose 25 percent 120 gives 150.
So the real wage is unchanged.
So the answer is No: her real wage stayed at 10,000 rupees.
